## Context / Problem
Found 2026-11-23 PST while fixing immoral-heated-doctorfish (Gerrit/Jira credentials in operator argv). `docs/mcp-client-setup.md` (lines 95 and 174) tells users to run `copilot mcp add ... --header "Authorization: Bearer $MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT"` and `claude mcp add ... --header "Authorization: Bearer ${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLAUDE}"`. The double quotes make the shell expand the PAT, so the rebar MCP client PAT is on the `copilot`/`claude` process command line while it runs, where any local user or process monitor can read it, and it is then written in clear into the client's config file.

This was kept out of immoral-heated-doctorfish because it is a different credential (the MCP client PAT, not a Gerrit or Jira credential) and the fix depends on each vendor CLI's handling of a literal `${VAR}` header placeholder, which needs checking against the Copilot CLI and Claude Code documentation.

## Vendor behaviour (checked 2026-11-23 PST)
- Claude Code (official MCP docs, code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp): `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` expand in a server's `url` and `headers` for project `.mcp.json` and for local/user entries in `~/.claude.json`; `claude mcp add-json <name> '<json>'` adds an entry from the command line. `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI` is not among the credential names Claude Code blanks in remote headers.
- GitHub Copilot CLI (installed 1.0.114): the official "Adding MCP servers" page is silent on expansion. The maintainer's closing comment on github/copilot-cli#1232 states `${VAR}` expansion works in MCP config value fields including HTTP headers, and changelog 1.0.108 says to "use ${NAME} to reference a host environment variable". The committed repository `.mcp.json`, which Copilot already reads, relies on `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}`.
- Shell: double quotes around `${VAR}` expand it before the CLI starts, so the PAT lands in argv and is then saved in clear in the client config.

## Approach
`docs/mcp-client-setup.md`:
- Copilot CLI: drop the `copilot mcp add ... --header "...$MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT"` command. The documented setup is the committed project `.mcp.json` (already `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}`); for a user-level fallback, copy or merge the `examples/mcp-clients/copilot/mcp-config.json` entry into `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`. The inline JSON snippet uses `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}`, the canonical name `rebar store doctor` checks for Copilot (`CANONICAL_PAT_ENV`), instead of the stale `$MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT`.
- Claude Code: the documented setup is the committed project `.mcp.json`. For the user-level fallback, replace the `claude mcp add ... --header "...${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLAUDE}"` command with `claude mcp add-json -s user rebar '<json>'` (explicit user scope, written to `~/.claude.json`), where the single-quoted JSON carries the literal `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}` placeholder that Claude Code expands at connect time; the JSON snippet uses `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}` too.
- Add a short warning: never pass the PAT as a double-quoted `--header` value, because the shell expands it into argv and the client saves the expanded value.
- Add the cleanup for anyone who already ran an old command, naming where each one saved the value. The old `claude mcp add` passed no `-s`, so Claude Code saved a local-scope entry for the directory it ran in (inside `~/.claude.json`): remove it with `claude mcp remove rebar -s local` from that directory (and `-s user` if it was added with `-s user`). The old `copilot mcp add` saved to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`: remove it with `copilot mcp remove rebar`. Then re-add the documented way, and ask the operator to rotate the PAT per `infra/runbooks/mcp-client-pats.md`, since it was exposed in argv and on disk. The doc does not claim `rebar store doctor` finds them (it reads only top-level `mcpServers` and skips home configs when a project `.mcp.json` exists).

Same class elsewhere, same fix:
- `examples/mcp-clients/claude/.mcp.json`: its `$comment` carries the double-quoted `claude mcp add --header` one-liner; switch it to the single-quoted `add-json` form. The `mcpServers` entry is unchanged.
- `examples/mcp-clients/copilot/mcp-config.json`: switch the header (and its `$comment`) from bare `$MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI` to braced `${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}`, the form the Copilot evidence above documents and the committed root `.mcp.json` already uses. `rebar store doctor`'s `_ENV_REF` accepts both forms.
- `docs/mcp-auth.md` (line 184, and the client table at line 327) recommends Claude Code `--header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"`, which puts the PAT in argv too; point it at the `headers` entry with a `${VAR}` placeholder / `claude mcp add-json` instead.

Guard, `tests/unit/test_review_bot_git_credential_argv.py`:
- Delete `_OPERATOR_EXCLUDED` (and its comment and use), so `_operator_files()` scans `docs/mcp-client-setup.md` with the existing patterns, unchanged; add the doc to `test_the_operator_scan_covers_the_files_named_by_the_bug`.
- The existing globs do not cover `examples/`, and the line-based `header-arg` pattern cannot see a command inside a JSON string (the quotes are escaped as `\"`). Add a test that parses every `examples/mcp-clients/**/*.json` file with `json.loads` (so they stay valid JSON), joins each `$comment` list into text, and asserts `_operator_hits` finds nothing; plus a case proving that test flags the old double-quoted one-liner when it is embedded in a `$comment`.
No new config key, environment variable, or flag; guard patterns are not loosened.

## Scope
- `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`
- `docs/mcp-auth.md` (the two Claude Code `--header` mentions)
- `examples/mcp-clients/claude/.mcp.json` (`$comment` only)
- `examples/mcp-clients/copilot/mcp-config.json` (header placeholder braced, `$comment` to match)
- `tests/unit/test_review_bot_git_credential_argv.py`

## Testing
- Run against the unfixed files first: with the exclusion removed and the doc unchanged, `test_no_operator_script_or_doc_puts_a_credential_in_argv` fails on `docs/mcp-client-setup.md` (`header-arg`); the new example-`$comment` test fails on `examples/mcp-clients/claude/.mcp.json`. Both pass after the rewrite.
- `test_the_operator_scan_covers_the_files_named_by_the_bug` asserts the doc is scanned, so the exclusion cannot silently return.
- Positive control: the new example test's helper flags a `$comment` containing `--header "Authorization: Bearer ${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}"`, so a passing scan is not a blind one.
- Manual check of the documented Claude Code command, done 2026-11-23 PST with Claude Code 2.1.311, no real PAT, and `HOME`/`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` pointed at a scratch directory so no user config is touched: `claude mcp add-json -s user` stored `"Authorization": "Bearer ${MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI}"` literally in the scratch `.claude.json`; a second user-scope entry pointing at a local HTTP listener, checked with `claude mcp list` under `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_CLI=dummy-not-a-pat-123`, made the listener receive `Bearer dummy-not-a-pat-123`, so the placeholder expands at connect time from user scope. Copilot's connect-time expansion is not exercised locally (it needs an authenticated session); its evidence is the vendor statements above and the committed root `.mcp.json`.
- `make verify` before push.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/mcp-client-setup.md` no longer shows a command that puts the expanded MCP client PAT in a process argv; the documented setup keeps the PAT out of argv (for example a literal `${VAR}` placeholder the client expands at connect time, verified against each client's documentation).
- [ ] The operator-credential argv guard added by immoral-heated-doctorfish scans `docs/mcp-client-setup.md` and passes.
